question_text: An arithmetic sequence has terms $u_7 = 1$ and $u_{15} = -23$.

subparts.stem: Find the first term $u_1$ and common difference $d$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up simultaneous equations using u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d

subparts.solution: $u_7 = 1 \implies u_1 + 6d = 1$ ...(1) and $u_{15} = -23 \implies u_1 + 14d = -23$ ...(2). Multiply both sides of (1) by $-1$: $-u_1 - 6d = -1$. Adding the equations: $8d = -24 \implies d = -3$. Substituting into (1): $u_1 + 6(-3) = 1 \implies u_1 - 18 = 1 \implies u_1 = 19$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The $n$-th term of an arithmetic sequence is $u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d$. Given two terms, set up a system of two linear equations in terms of $u_1$ and $d$.
step_by_step: Subtract the first equation from the second: $8d = -24 \implies d = -3$.
Substitute $d = -3$ back into the first equation to solve for $u_1 = 19$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Arithmetic errors when subtracting negative numbers (e.g., $-23 - 1 = -24$).

mark_breakdown.desc: Substituting u_1 and d into the formula for u_27

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use the general formula $u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d$ with the values of $u_1$ and $d$ found in part a.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using $n$ instead of $n - 1$ (multiplying by 27 instead of 26).

subparts.stem: Find the sum of the first 27 terms of the series.

mark_breakdown.desc: Applying the formula S_n = n/2(u_1 + u_n)

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression can be computed directly using the first and last terms: $S_n = \frac{n}{2}(u_1 + u_n)$.
step_by_step: Substitute $n = 27$, $u_1 = 19$, and $u_{27} = -59$ into the sum formula.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Sign errors during addition inside parentheses: $19 + (-59) = -40$.
